steps.description: Run the filtered TPM matrix through immunedeconv with four methods: (a) EPIC — absolute fractions including the uncharacterized (mostly tumor) share; (b) quanTIseq — absolute fractions of its ten TIL10 immune types; (c) MCP-counter — abundance scores of immune and stromal populations (on the log2 TPM input); (d) xCell — 64-type enrichment scores. This is a human melanoma dataset matched to blood/tumor-derived reference profiles; state the reference-tissue match. CIBERSORT (LM22 tool of record) and ESTIMATE (purity tool of record) are absent from the package pool — no LM22 proportion or tumor purity is claimed; quanTIseq/EPIC fractions stand in for proportions with their differing cell-type sets stated, and xCell immune/stroma scores are named as relative stand-ins for the ESTIMATE scores. Per R-0128, a composition claim about a cell type is made only when >=2 methods agree on the direction of the between-group difference; report all four methods' estimates side by side in one long table (method, cell type, sample, score). Cell composition here is the OUTCOME of the analysis, not a covariate of a DE design — there is no separate DE question in this run.

steps.description: For each method's cell-type-by-sample estimate matrix from T3S2, fit one limma linear model per cell type with condition (treated vs untreated) as the only covariate. Transform scores to log scale first: log2(x + 1) for MCP-counter abundance and xCell enrichment scores; log2(fraction + 1e-3) for EPIC and quanTIseq fractions (raw proportions violate the linear-model homoscedasticity assumption near 0). plan.title: Melanoma anti-PD-1: TME deconvolution from TPM
plan.analytical_narrative: The question asks for the immune and stromal composition of each of the 12 melanoma biopsies (6 anti-PD-1 treated vs 6 untreated) and whether composition differs between groups. Only a gene-level TPM table (12000 genes x 12 samples, Salmon, HGNC symbols) was delivered — no raw counts and no quantification directories — so count-based models (DESeq2/edgeR) and count-based deconvolution modes are off the table; the TPM scale is exactly the input the linear-scale deconvolution methods expect. The plan therefore: (1) runs sample-structure QC on log2 TPM, explicitly inspecting sample_01 which was sequenced at ~1/4 of median depth (kept per low-depth policy, since TPM is already depth-normalized but low depth means fewer detected genes and noisier estimates); (2) applies the TPM low-abundance filter (>=1 TPM in >=6 samples) to remove genes that only add noise to the mixture; (3) estimates cell composition with four complementary methods through the common immunedeconv interface — EPIC (absolute fractions incl. uncharacterized/tumor share), quanTIseq (absolute fractions of the ten TIL10 immune types), MCP-counter (abundance scores of immune AND stromal populations), and xCell (64-type enrichment scores) — with composition claims made only where >=2 methods agree in direction; (4) tests treated vs control per cell type with limma moderated t-tests on log2-transformed score matrices, BH FDR within each method, plus a sensitivity rerun excluding sample_01; (5) reports the per-sample composition table, the group comparison, and a reproducibility record. CIBERSORT/LM22 and ESTIMATE are not available in this environment, so no LM22-proportion or tumor-purity claim is made; quanTIseq/EPIC fractions stand in for proportions with their cell-type set stated, and xCell immune/stroma scores are named as relative stand-ins.
